| SPR trend recovered in a rebuild (sigmaF 0.3) | 27% | ~50% |
| Linf input 0.9 / 1.1 x true | +91 / -40% | +74 / -28% |

The cut halves the CVL sensitivity, removes the bias of a strong unmodelled dome
and roughly doubles responsiveness; it costs a small positive bias (+7 to +10%)
and more noise under stable F, and does not remove the Linf sensitivity.
Starting value: 0.80-0.85 x Linf, fixed across fits.

## Plus group, robust likelihood, GTG range

- `Lplus = L` pools bins with lower bound $\geq L$ into one (the total counts, the
  shape does not).
- `rob_eps = 0.001` bounds the cost of a few fish in bins the model barely reaches.
- The largest growth group stops at $L_\infty(1 + \text{maxsd}\cdot\text{CVL})$; with
  `maxsd = 2` the effective CV is about 0.9 x CVL. Fish beyond it get near-zero
  probability; a tail cut makes this irrelevant.

# Model equations and comparison of models

## Fishing mortality and total mortality

$F_{g,y}(L) = F_{g,y} S_g(L)$, $Z_y(L) = M(L) + \sum_g F_{g,y}(L)$. Gear shares of F
are informed by `catch_by_gear` through a soft constraint on the predicted
catch shares (`catch.sd`, default 0.05), in weight by default:
$$
\log\frac{\hat C^w_{g,y}}{\hat C^w_{G,y}} \sim N\!\left(\log\frac{c_{g,y}}{c_{G,y}},\ \texttt{catch.sd}^2\right),
\qquad \hat C^w_{g,y} = \sum_L C_{g,y}(L)\, W(L),
$$
where $c_{g,y}$ is `catch_by_gear` and $G$ the last gear. The predicted shares
are in `fit$report$catch_share`. With `settings$catch_units = "numbers"` the
shares are compared in numbers, $\hat C_{g,y} = \sum_L C_{g,y}(L)$, as in
fishblicc (Medley 2025); use this when the catch split is known in numbers.

## Expected catch and length composition

FLicc separates the **population model** (expected numbers at length under
growth, M, F and selectivity) from the **observation model** (the likelihood
that links the observed counts to the expected composition), so either can be
changed without the other. With $N_i$ the expected number of fish entering
length bin $i$, the expected catch of gear $g$ in bin $i$ is
$$
C_{i,g} = \frac{F_{i,g}}{Z_i}\left(N_i - N_{i+1}\right), \qquad Z_i = M_i + \sum_g F_{i,g},
$$
and the expected composition of gear $g$ is $\pi_{i,g} = C_{i,g} / \sum_i C_{i,g}$.

## Population model

`pop_model = "gtg"` (default, as LBSPR): growth-type groups
$L_{\infty,h} = L_\infty(1 + \mathrm{CVL}\, z_h)$, $z_h$ on
`seq(-maxsd, maxsd, length = ngtg)` (13 groups, `maxsd = 2`), weights
$\omega_h \propto \phi(z_h)$. Within a group, survival across bin $i$ follows from
the time needed to grow through it under von Bertalanffy growth:
$$
N_{i+1,h} = N_{i,h}\left(\frac{L_{\infty,h} - L_{i+1}}{L_{\infty,h} - L_i}\right)^{Z_i/k},
\qquad N_i = \sum_h \omega_h N_{i,h}.
$$

`pop_model = "gamma"` follows fishblicc: Linf is gamma-distributed among
individuals, and the numbers at length integrate survival over that distribution,
$$
N_i = \int f(L_\infty)\, S_i(L_\infty)\, dL_\infty ,
$$
evaluated by Gauss-Laguerre quadrature (slower). Both are equilibrium models:
each year is explained by the equilibrium at that year's F (section *Lag under
changing F* on the consequences).

## Observation model

For gear $g$ in year $y$, with counts $\mathbf y_{g,y}$ and total $n_{g,y}$:

- `obs_model = "mn"` (default): $\mathbf y_{g,y} \sim \text{Multinomial}(n_{g,y}, \boldsymbol\pi_{g,y})$.
- `"nb"`: $y_{i,g,y} \sim \text{NB}(\mu, \phi)$ with $\mu = n_{g,y}\pi_{i,g,y}$ and
  $\text{Var} = \mu + \mu^2/\phi$; $\phi$ is estimated.
- `"dm"`: $\mathbf y_{g,y} \sim \text{Dirichlet-multinomial}(n_{g,y}, \alpha_0 \boldsymbol\pi_{g,y})$
  with $\alpha_0 = n_{g,y}$ (`dm_theta = "fixed"`) or estimated (`"linear"`,
  `"saturating"`).

How the sample size enters each of them is explained in section *Effective
sample size and observation models*; the models are compared on the same data
below.

## Comparison of models

The population model (`gtg` or `gamma`) and the observation model (`mn`, `dm`,
`nb`) can be combined freely. The four fits below differ only in these two
settings; `Map()` runs one fit per list of settings.

```{r model-compare, fig.height = 4}
model_settings <- list(
  gtg_mn   = list(CVL = 0.1, pop_model = "gtg",   obs_model = "mn"),
  gtg_dm   = list(CVL = 0.1, pop_model = "gtg",   obs_model = "dm", dm_theta = "saturating"),
  gtg_nb   = list(CVL = 0.1, pop_model = "gtg",   obs_model = "nb"),
  gamma_nb = list(CVL = 0.1, pop_model = "gamma", obs_model = "nb"))   # as fishblicc

fits_model <- Map(function(set) {
  fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = sel_fun, catch_by_gear = cbg, settings = set)
}, model_settings)

data.frame(model    = names(fits_model),
           SPR_last = round(sapply(fits_model, sprcur_flicc), 3),
           se_log   = round(sapply(fits_model, se_logspr), 3),
           row.names = NULL)
plot_spr(fits_model, ci = TRUE)
```

The gamma model integrates over Linf numerically and is slower:

```{r model-time}
system.time(fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = sel_fun, catch_by_gear = cbg,
                   settings = model_settings$gtg_nb))
system.time(fiticc(lfd, stklen, sel_fun = sel_fun, catch_by_gear = cbg,
                   settings = model_settings$gamma_nb))
```

Log-likelihoods and AIC are not comparable between observation models (they are
likelihoods of different things); compare the estimates, their precision and the
fit to the compositions (`plot_len`). Differences between `gtg` and `gamma` show
the sensitivity to the approximation of growth variability, differences between
`mn`, `dm` and `nb` the weight and robustness given to the compositions.

| Purpose | `pop_model` | `obs_model` | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routine assessment, MSE | `"gtg"` | `"dm"` | fast; robust with real data |
| LBSPR-style | `"gtg"` | `"mn"` | fastest; sensitive to the ESS; LBSPR fits each year separately (`by_year = TRUE`) with Linf, M/k and CVL fixed |
| LBB | `"gtg"`, `ngtg = 1` | `"dm"`, fixed precision | `lbb_flicc()`; [Reproducing LBB](#repro-lbb) |
| fishblicc replication | `"gamma"` | `"nb"` | slower; closest to fishblicc |

# Reproducing LBSPR, LBB and fishblicc {#reproduce}

Each of the three tools is a configuration of FLicc (table in section *FLicc: a
framework for length-interval catch curves*). This section fits each tool's
configuration to the tool's own example data, compares the results with the
tool's published output, and adds FLicc's default for comparison.

## LBSPR: the multi-year example {#repro-lbspr}

LBSPR (Hordyk et al. 2015, 2016) fits the GTG model (13 growth-type groups, CV
of Linf 0.1, groups over $\pm 2$ SD) with a multinomial likelihood to each year
separately, with Linf, M/k and CVL fixed, and estimates SL50, SL95 and F/M
(apical F over M) by year. The example is LBSPR's multi-year length-frequency
file `LFreq_MultiYrHead.csv` (six years, 5-mm classes, mid-points given) with the
life history of LBSPR's vignette: Linf = 100 mm, M/k = 1.5, L50 = 66 mm,
L95 = 70 mm. The data are entered directly:

```{r lbspr-data}
lbspr_csv <- "
Length,2010,2011,2012,2013,2014,2015
2.5,0,0,0,0,0,0
7.5,0,0,0,0,0,0
12.5,0,0,0,0,0,0
17.5,0,6,0,0,0,0
22.5,0,0,0,0,0,0
27.5,6,6,6,0,0,6
32.5,0,6,6,18,12,18
37.5,36,42,30,60,30,36
42.5,78,96,66,42,66,78
47.5,126,102,126,102,114,150
52.5,156,174,222,192,174,180
57.5,252,246,216,228,288,198
62.5,192,192,144,174,234,168
67.5,126,162,150,180,156,168
72.5,180,138,210,114,108,132
77.5,138,84,114,132,78,90
82.5,48,72,66,78,108,96
87.5,36,48,30,48,24,48
92.5,42,24,24,42,24,36
97.5,6,24,12,12,0,24
102.5,12,12,12,12,18,0
107.5,0,0,0,0,0,6
112.5,0,0,0,0,0,0
117.5,0,0,0,0,0,0
122.5,0,0,0,0,0,0
127.5,0,0,0,0,0,0"
lb <- read.csv(text = lbspr_csv, check.names = FALSE)
lfd_lbspr <- FLQuants(Example = FLQuant(as.matrix(lb[, -1]),
                      dimnames = list(len = lb$Length - 2.5, year = names(lb)[-1]), units = "mm"))
# k only scales F and M; F/M and SPR depend on M/k = 1.5 only
lhpar_lbspr <- FLPar(linf = 100, k = 0.2, M = 0.3, L50 = 66, L95 = 70, a = 1e-5, b = 3)
stk_lbspr <- stocklen(lfd_lbspr, lhpar_lbspr, m_model = "constant")
```

Three fits: LBSPR's configuration (multinomial, each year separately), the same
likelihood with all years fitted jointly (one selectivity, random walk on F), and
FLicc's default (Dirichlet-multinomial with estimated precision, years jointly).
For the separate years `Map()` fits one model per year:

```{r lbspr-fits}
set_lbspr <- list(CVL = 0.1, ngtg = 13, maxsd = 2, obs_model = "mn")
yrs_lbspr <- dimnames(stk_lbspr)$year
fits_lbspr_y <- Map(function(y) {
  lfd_y <- FLQuants(lapply(lfd_lbspr, function(x) x[, y]))
  fiticc(lfd_y, stocklen(lfd_y, lhpar_lbspr, m_model = "constant"), sel_fun = "logistic",
         catch_by_gear = 1, settings = set_lbspr, verbose = FALSE)
}, yrs_lbspr)
fit_lbspr_j <- fiticc(lfd_lbspr, stk_lbspr, sel_fun = "logistic", catch_by_gear = 1,
                      settings = set_lbspr)
fit_lbspr_d <- fiticc(lfd_lbspr, stk_lbspr, sel_fun = "logistic", catch_by_gear = 1,
                      settings = list(CVL = 0.1))
```

LBSPR's results for these data (`LBSPRfit()`, smoothed estimates `@Ests`) are
entered as a table; the FLicc estimates are taken from the fits (selectivity
from the parameters, F/M as apical F over M, SPR):

```{r lbspr-compare}
lbspr_out <- data.frame(year = 2010:2015,
                        SL50 = c(48.69, 48.70, 48.69, 48.70, 48.63, 48.42),
                        SL95 = c(62.82, 62.88, 62.76, 62.78, 62.60, 62.34),
                        FM   = c(0.55, 0.55, 0.55, 0.55, 0.55, 0.54),
                        SPR  = c(0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.45, 0.45, 0.45))
est_flicc <- function(f) {
  sm <- exp(f$obj$env$parList(par = f$obj$env$last.par.best)$Sm) * 100   # relative to Linf
  data.frame(year = as.numeric(f$tmb_data$year_names), SL50 = sm[1], SL95 = sm[1] + sm[2],
             FM = as.numeric(f$report$Fap) / 0.3, SPR = as.numeric(f$report$spr))
}
lbspr_runs <- list("LBSPR" = lbspr_out,
                   "FLicc mn, by year" = do.call(rbind, lapply(fits_lbspr_y, est_flicc)),
                   "FLicc mn, joint" = est_flicc(fit_lbspr_j),
                   "FLicc default" = est_flicc(fit_lbspr_d))
lbspr_tab <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(x, nm) cbind(run = nm, round(x, 3)), lbspr_runs, names(lbspr_runs)))
rownames(lbspr_tab) <- NULL
lbspr_tab
```

```{r lbspr-plot, fig.height = 3.5}
lbspr_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("SL50", "FM", "SPR"), function(v)
  data.frame(lbspr_tab[, c("run", "year")], what = v, value = lbspr_tab[[v]])))
lbspr_long$run <- factor(lbspr_long$run, levels = names(lbspr_runs))
ggplot(lbspr_long, aes(year, value, colour = run)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~what, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("black", "#E69F00", "#0072B2", "#009E73")) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = NULL, colour = NULL) + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
plot_spr(fit_lbspr_d, ci = TRUE)
```

With LBSPR's configuration (`obs_model = "mn"`, each year separately) FLicc gives
SL50, F/M and SPR close to LBSPR's: mean SPR
`r round(mean(lbspr_runs[["FLicc mn, by year"]]$SPR), 3)` against
`r round(mean(lbspr_out$SPR), 3)`. LBSPR's estimates shown are smoothed over the
years (Kalman filter), FLicc's separate fits are not. Fitting the years jointly
gives one selectivity and smoother F; the default likelihood estimates how much
weight the compositions carry and widens the intervals accordingly.

## LBB: the Illex example {#repro-lbb}

### LBB as a special case of the GTG model

LBB (Froese et al. 2018) describes the numbers surviving to length class $j$
(lower bound $L_j$) with one growth type,
$$
N_j = N_{j-1}\left(\frac{L_\infty - L_j}{L_\infty - L_{j-1}}\right)^{M/K + (F/K)\,S_j},
$$
where $S_j$ is a logistic selectivity with length at 50% selection $L_c$ and
slope $\alpha$ (relative to $L_\infty$). This is FLicc's GTG recursion with a
single growth-type group (`pop_model = "gtg"`, `ngtg = 1`). Each year is fitted
separately, with a prior on Linf (CV at most 1%, from an `nls()` fit to the
aggregated frequencies, or a user value), on M/K (1.5, SD 0.15) and, in LBB,
also on $L_c$ and $\alpha$; the likelihood is a Dirichlet on the relative
frequencies with a concentration of $10^4$.

The expected catch in a length class can be computed in two ways:

- **with the pile-up correction** (Hordyk et al. 2019; FLicc's model and LBB
  with `Pile = 1`): the numbers in the class are the survivors integrated over
  the time spent in it, $C_j \propto S_j\,(N_j - N_{j+1})/(M/K + (F/K) S_j)$.
  Fish grow more slowly towards Linf, so they accumulate in the large classes;
- **without it** (LBB `Pile = 0`, the setting of LBB's example stocks): the
  catch is proportional to the survivorship at the class bound,
  $C_j \propto S_j N_j$.

`lbb_flicc()` sets FLicc up as LBB: one growth type, one gear (gears pooled),
Linf and M/K priors from `lbb_priors_flicc()` (LBB's guess step) or user values,
lengths at or above the Linf prior excluded, and each year fitted separately
(`by_year = TRUE`) or jointly with a random walk on F (`by_year = FALSE`). The
options `pile` (LBB's `Pile`) and `ess` (data weighting; `ess = 20000` with a
fixed Dirichlet-multinomial precision corresponds to LBB's concentration of
$10^4$) allow LBB's settings to be matched. Selectivity is estimated without
priors. `lbbref_flicc()` gives LBB's quantities by year (Linf, Lc, M/K, F/K,
F/M, Z/K, Lopt, Lc_opt, B/B0 from LBB's Beverton-Holt equations) next to
FLicc's EPR and SPR, and `plot_lbb()` LBB's summary figure.

### The Illex fit

The example uses LBB's own example stock *Illex coindetii* (Adriatic) with the
settings of LBB's `Example_ID.csv`: the years 1996, 1999, 2001, 2002, 2009,
2014 and 2016, Linf set to 23 cm, Lm50 16 cm and `Pile = 0`. The data are read
from the LBB repository (lengths in mm, converted to cm) and raised to 1000 per
year:

```{r lbb-data}
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SISTA16/LBB/master/Example_Dat.csv"
lbb_dat <- tryCatch(read.csv(url), error = function(e) NULL)
have_lbb <- !is.null(lbb_dat)
if (have_lbb) {
  d <- subset(lbb_dat, Stock == "Ille_coi_AD" & !is.na(CatchNo))
  d <- aggregate(CatchNo ~ Year + Length, data = d, FUN = sum)
  d$data <- d$CatchNo / ave(d$CatchNo, d$Year, FUN = sum) * 1000
  lfd_illex <- FLQuantLen(lfd_long_to_wide(data.frame(len = d$Length / 10, year = d$Year,
                                                      data = d$data, qname = "Illex")),
                          unit = "cm", midL = FALSE)
}
yrs_illex <- c(1996, 1999, 2001, 2002, 2009, 2014, 2016)
```

Three fits: LBB's settings (`pile = 0`, LBB's data weighting), the same with
the pile-up correction, and FLicc's joint fit of all years with the
pile-up correction and the estimated Dirichlet-multinomial precision:

```{r lbb-fits, eval = have_lbb}
fit_lbb0 <- lbb_flicc(lfd_illex, Linf = 23, Lm50 = 16, years = yrs_illex,
                      pile = 0, ess = 20000)
fit_lbb1 <- lbb_flicc(lfd_illex, Linf = 23, Lm50 = 16, years = yrs_illex,
                      pile = 1, ess = 20000)
fit_lbbj <- lbb_flicc(lfd_illex, Linf = 23, Lm50 = 16, years = yrs_illex,
                      by_year = FALSE)
fit_lbb0
```

LBB's own results for this stock (`LBB_33a.R`, MCMC medians) are entered as a
table and compared by year:

```{r lbb-compare, eval = have_lbb, fig.height = 4.5}
lbb_out <- data.frame(year = yrs_illex,
                      ZK  = c(2.32, 3.12, 2.57, 3.72, 3.15, 5.24, 6.85),
                      FM  = c(0.265, 0.878, 0.732, 1.467, 0.910, 2.713, 3.570),
                      BB0 = c(0.699, 0.267, 0.293, 0.138, 0.294, 0.065, 0.044))
runs <- list("LBB (JAGS)" = lbb_out, "FLicc, Pile = 0" = fit_lbb0$table,
             "FLicc, Pile = 1" = fit_lbb1$table, "FLicc, Pile = 1, joint" = fit_lbbj$table)
cmp <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(x, nm) data.frame(run = nm, year = x$year, ZK = x$ZK,
                                                     FM = x$FM, BB0 = x$BB0), runs, names(runs)))
cmp$run <- factor(cmp$run, levels = names(runs))
long <- rbind(data.frame(cmp[, 1:2], what = "Z/K", value = cmp$ZK),
              data.frame(cmp[, 1:2], what = "F/M", value = cmp$FM),
              data.frame(cmp[, 1:2], what = "B/B0", value = cmp$BB0))
ggplot(long, aes(year, value, colour = run)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~what, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("black", "#E69F00", "#0072B2", "#009E73")) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
dif <- function(x) round(mean(x$ZK - lbb_out$ZK), 2)
```

The same comparison with `plot_epr()` and `plot_spr()`: LBB's B/B0 next to
FLicc's exploitable potential ratio (EPR, the same quantity from the FLicc
engine), with LBB's reference points (B/B0 at F = M and Lc = Lc_opt, a proxy for
Bmsy/B0, and half of it), and FLicc's SPR, which LBB does not report:

```{r lbb-epr-spr, eval = have_lbb, fig.height = 3.5}
yr_flq <- function(tab, col) FLQuant(matrix(tab[[col]], nrow = 1), dimnames = list(year = tab$year))
bfm <- attr(fit_lbb1$table, "BFM1B0")
plot_epr(FLQuants("LBB (JAGS)" = yr_flq(lbb_out, "BB0"),
                  "FLicc, Pile = 0" = yr_flq(fit_lbb0$table, "EPR"),
                  "FLicc, Pile = 1" = yr_flq(fit_lbb1$table, "EPR"),
                  "FLicc, Pile = 1, joint" = yr_flq(fit_lbbj$table, "EPR")),
         ref_levels = c(bfm, bfm / 2), title = "B/B0 (LBB) and EPR (FLicc)")
plot_spr(FLQuants("FLicc, Pile = 0" = yr_flq(fit_lbb0$table, "SPR"),
                  "FLicc, Pile = 1" = yr_flq(fit_lbb1$table, "SPR"),
                  "FLicc, Pile = 1, joint" = yr_flq(fit_lbbj$table, "SPR")))
```

With LBB's settings (`pile = 0`) FLicc reproduces LBB: Z/K differs from LBB's
by `r if (have_lbb) dif(fit_lbb0$table) else NA` on average over the years, and
F/M and B/B0 follow LBB's estimates year by year. The remaining differences are
small: LBB's priors on $\alpha$ and F/K shape how Z/K is split into M/K and F/K
(LBB's M/K moves between 1.4 and 1.8 across years, FLicc's stays near the prior
of 1.5), and MCMC medians differ slightly from maximum likelihood estimates.

With the pile-up correction, Z/K is higher by
`r if (have_lbb) dif(fit_lbb1$table) else NA` on average, so F/M is higher and
B/B0 lower. Survivorship declines as about $(L_\infty - L)^{Z/K}$, while the
numbers in a class decline as about $(L_\infty - L)^{Z/K - 1}$, so the model
without the correction needs a Z/K about one unit lower to describe the same
frequencies. The joint fit of all years (`by_year = FALSE`) shares selectivity
and links F between years, which smooths the year-to-year changes in the
separate fits.

```{r lbb-plot, eval = have_lbb, fig.height = 7}
plot_lbb(fit_lbb1)
```

### Points to consider with LBB

- **Pile-up correction.** Hordyk et al. (2019) pointed out that the numbers in a
  length class are the survivors integrated over the class, and that without
  the correction F is underestimated. Froese et al. (2019) argued that the
  correction matters most for continuous recruitment and sampling, and added it
  as an option to LBB. In LBB's B/B0, computed from the Beverton-Holt equations,
  the integration is included; with `Pile = 0` Z/K is therefore estimated with
  a different model from the one used for B/B0. FLicc uses the integrated
  numbers for estimation and status (`pile = 1`, default); `pile = 0` is
  available to reproduce LBB.
- **Priors.** LBB's priors on $L_c$ and in particular on $\alpha$ (SD 2.5%,
  centred on a value derived from each year's ascending limb) fix much of the
  selectivity shape; together with the M/K prior they determine the split of
  Z/K into M/K and F/K, which the data alone barely inform. In FLicc these
  constraints are optional settings (priors, `sel_fixed`).
- **Separate years.** Fitting each year separately lets selectivity and Linf
  change between years, which absorbs recruitment pulses as apparent changes in
  selectivity. The joint fit (`by_year = FALSE`) estimates one selectivity and
  links F between years.
- **Weighting.** LBB's Dirichlet concentration of $10^4$ gives the data a weight
  close to $10^4$ fish per year whatever the sample size; FLicc's default
  estimates the precision from the data.

Within these choices, LBB's estimates can be reproduced in FLicc, and each
assumption can be switched separately to see its effect.

## fishblicc: the Bombay duck example {#repro-fishblicc}

FLicc includes the Bombay duck example of fishblicc (three gears) to check
consistency with fishblicc. Natural mortality decreases with length
(`m_model = "inverse"`, $M(L) = M\, L_{ref} / L$ with $L_{ref} = 21.9$), and
Linf, M/k and CVL are estimated with priors as in fishblicc. fishblicc
compares the relative catch of each gear in numbers of fish (Medley 2025), so
the catch shares are given in numbers here (`catch_units = "numbers"`):

```{r fishblicc-data}
data("fishblicc_example")
lhpar_fishblicc <- rbind(lhpar_fishblicc,
                         FLPar(M = lhpar_fishblicc["k"] * lhpar_fishblicc["Mk"]))
stklen_fishblicc <- stocklen(lfd_fishblicc, lhpar_fishblicc,
                             m_model = "inverse", reflen = 21.9)
```

```{r fishblicc-fit}
fit_fishblicc <- fiticc(lfd_fishblicc, stklen_fishblicc,
                        sel_fun = c("dsnormal", "dsnormal", "dsnormal"),
                        catch_by_gear = c(0.1802070, 0.2101353, 0.6096577),
                        settings = list(pop_model = "gamma", obs_model = "nb",
                                        CVL = 0.14, CVL.sd = 0.1,
                                        linf.sd = 2 / 40, Mk.sd = 0.1,
                                        catch_units = "numbers"))
flicc_convergence(fit_fishblicc)
sprcur_flicc(fit_fishblicc)
```

```{r fishblicc-plots, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_sel(fit_fishblicc)
plot_len(fit_fishblicc, by_gear = TRUE)
```

```{r fishblicc-eq, fig.height = 5}
eqstk_fishblicc <- eqstklen(fit_fishblicc, s = 0.7)
eqstk_fishblicc@refpts
plot_eqcurves(eqstk_fishblicc)
```

# Part III: Management {.unnumbered .part}

# Use in an MSE

`flicc.sa()` wraps `fiticc()` as the estimation step of an `mse` management
procedure, with `lbi.hcr()`, `rfb.flicc.hcr()` and `flicc.is()` for the
harvest control rule and implementation:

```{r mse, eval = FALSE}
est <- mseCtrl(method = flicc.sa, args = list(
  lhpar = lhpar, sel_fun = sel_fun, ess.g = NULL,   # raw counts
  settings = list(obs_model = "dm", dm_theta = "saturating", CVL = 0.1,
                  sigmaF = 0.3,      # fixed (or the F_re estimate from the real data)
                  tail_cut = 47,     # absolute length, the same in every iteration
                  spr_ref = 40),
  spr = 40))
```

- `se = FALSE` is used inside `flicc.sa()`; fixed sigmaF avoids its estimation in
  every year and iteration.
- The tail cut and sigmaF both trade responsiveness against stability; tune them
  together with the smoothing of the harvest control rule.
- Expect the equilibrium model to be pessimistic during a rebuild and optimistic
  while F increases.

# Summary of checks and recommendations

| # | Check | Red flag | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | sample size by gear-year (`plot_lfdn`) | < 50 fish or < 10 bins; gear mix changing | ESS per gear; drop/pool poor gear-years |
| 2 | composition consistency (`plot_lfd`) | shifts in mode or left limb | split gears/periods; restrict years |
| 3 | largest fish vs Linf | > 1% at or above Linf | revisit Linf; tail cut |
| 4 | empirical catch curves (`plot_zlcc`) | curved limbs, jumping slopes | dome or tail cut; keep random walk |
| 5 | life-history inputs | Linf inconsistent with data; odd M/k | Linf sensitivity; priors (`linf.sd`) as a check |
| 6 | selectivity plausibility (`plot_sel`) | narrow or unsupported domes | logistic; fix from external data; dome sensitivity (`dome_sens_flicc`) |
| 7 | convergence (`flicc_convergence`) | gradient, Hessian, bounds | restarts; simplify; tail cut |
| 8 | fit to compositions (`plot_len`, `plot_resid_bubble`, `lmean_resid_flicc`, `ppc_flicc`) | systematic misfit; failed runs test; many values outside predictive intervals | selectivity, Linf, tail cut; lower ESS; cohort patterns are expected |
| 9 | retrospective | rho beyond ±0.2 | trends in selectivity or sampling |
| 10 | indicators vs status | gears disagree | best gear; pooling; HCR smoothing |

| Topic | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Observation model | `dm` with real data |
| Sample size | `dm` with `dm_theta = "saturating"` on raw counts or ESS >= 500 (the data set their weight); with fixed precision or `mn`, ESS about 150-200 per gear-year, never raw thousands |
| Growth | fix Linf and CVL; Linf is the main sensitivity; `maxsd = 3` as sensitivity |
| Selectivity | logistic unless supported; always run `dome_sens_flicc()` (rsd 1000 to 0.4 x Linf) |
| Management options | `plot_contour_flicc()`: yield and SPR (or SSB with `s`) over selectivity and F by gear |
| F over time | random walk, sigmaF fixed (0.3 or the `F_re` estimate); `by_year = TRUE` only as a check |
| Tail | `tail_cut` at about 0.80-0.85 x Linf, as a length |
| Missing data | keep zeros, rely on the random walk; not without random walk |
| Status | SPR at the year's F; `s` for $B/B_{tgt}$ under Beverton-Holt; `plot_LBAdvice(flicc2FLStockR(fit))` |
| Models | `gtg` + `dm` routinely; `gamma` + `nb` to replicate fishblicc |
| MSE | fixed sigmaF, absolute tail cut, `se = FALSE`; tune with the HCR |

*Planned: a worked example of a rebuilding stock, refitted year by year, to show
how SPR, the tail cut and sigmaF respond over time; estimated Dirichlet-multinomial
overdispersion.*
